candidates.decision_relevance: Would resolve repeated cross-horizon disagreement and establish whether breadth, flow, funding, open interest, liquidation activity, and relative performance led or followed price changes.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily Director Outputs dated 2026-09-06 through 2026-09-09 repeatedly report unavailable 1-hour anchors, zero-span or materially shortened nominal windows, and unknown timestamp order.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamp-aligned BTC/ETH/ETH-BTC price, flow, funding, open-interest, liquidation, and breadth sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied snapshots cannot distinguish transient shocks, persistent deterioration, and subsequent re-acceleration because comparable hourly observations and exact event ordering are missing.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would test whether repeated proxy-breadth deterioration or improvement represented durable participation changes rather than endpoint movement or changing-universe effects.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W33-W36 and multiple daily outputs identify point-in-time top-100 breadth as proxy-only, with changing membership hashes and no durable breadth path.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Current breadth observations are not comparable enough to determine persistence, broadening, narrowing, or whether ETH leadership was accompanied by wider participation.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would separate healthy deleveraging from forced long liquidation, short covering, or renewed leverage build and clarify whether liquidity stress preceded subsequent price weakness.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W35-W36 and daily outputs repeatedly state that liquidation data are lower bounds, open-interest changes are directionally ambiguous, and positioning composition is unavailable.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Aggregate deleveraging and liquidation totals do not reveal long/short composition, venue completeness, or whether leverage normalization was followed by recovery or continued deterioration.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would show whether reported settled ETF demand was persistent and whether inflows translated into price, breadth, and liquidity support rather than being a one-session or stale observation.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly note that ETF context is settled only through isolated prior sessions, commonly 2026-09-04 or 2026-09-08, and lacks a trend or current-session sequence.
candidates.metric_name: Settled BTC/ETH ETF flow history with session timestamps
candidates.missing_history_problem: Single-session settled totals cannot resolve whether ETF demand offset deterioration, was concentrated, or failed to transmit into broader participation and price support.
